chapters.label: THE CHOICE
chapters.title: A quieter waterfall, with a rougher little approach
chapters.body: Discover Laos describes Tad Champee as less frequented than the plateau's headline falls. The access leaves Route 23 opposite the Tad Fane road, follows a signed side road, then drops from the parking area on a simple path and handcrafted stairs. The reward is not another huge panorama but a closer, quieter forest-and-stream setting.

note.label: USEFUL CHOICE
note.text: If Tad Fane gives you the photograph, Tad Champee gives you the pause.

items.label: Access

items.label: Walking
items.detail: The simple stairs and path deserve more care when wet.

items.label: Time & entry
items.detail: Enough for the side road, descent and a real pause by the waterfall. Confirm the current local fee.

faq.question: Why choose Tad Champee over Tad Fane or Tad Yuang?
faq.answer: Choose it for a quieter, closer forest stop. Tad Fane is about scale across a gorge and Tad Yuang about several waterfall viewpoints; Tad Champee is the slower alternative.

faq.question: How do I reach Tad Champee?
faq.answer: The official destination page places the access from Route 23 opposite the Tad Fane approach. Follow the signed side road for the final few kilometres.

faq.question: How much time should I allow?
faq.answer: One to two hours is comfortable once you include the side road and the walk down from the parking area.

faq.question: Is the walk difficult?
faq.answer: It is a short descent rather than a major hike, but the stairs are simple and can be slippery in wet conditions. Give yourself daylight and do not rush the return.
